Definition: to cover (with a garment); figuratively, to act covertly; by implication, to pillage
BiblicalUsage: Bagad means to deal treacherously — to act covertly, to cover a wrong with a garment of friendship. Hosea says they have dealt treacherously against the Lord, Isaiah says the treacherous dealers have dealt very treacherously, Malachi says Judah has dealt treacherously with the wife of his youth, and Proverbs says the transgressors shall be taken in their own naughtiness. Treachery is sin that smiles while it stabs.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe treachery is the ugliest sin because it wears a friend's face. I hold that the only cure is the plain dealing Proverbs promises: the integrity of the upright shall guide them.
